dealer_rule.text: NAFDAC has said crop-protection products may be sold only through NAFDAC-approved or accredited agrochemical dealers, and that dealers must be listed.

source.name: The Guardian Nigeria: NAFDAC moves to avert dangers of pesticides, agrochemical usage

checklist.text: Buy from a shop that sells agrochemicals as its business, and ask whether it is an approved or accredited dealer. Avoid open-market hawkers and unlabelled refills.

The pack must have a printed label in English with the product name, active ingredient, manufacturer, batch number, expiry date and a NAFDAC registration number. No label, or a label that is peeling or stuck on crooked, is a warning sign.
The pack should be sealed and undamaged. Do not buy opened, repacked or decanted products.
Check the expiry date and that the batch number on the pack matches the one on the label.
A price far below what other shops charge for the same product is a warning sign.
Ask for a receipt that names the product and the shop, and keep it with a photo of the pack and batch number. You need this to report a problem.

For fertiliser, check the bag is stitched and printed, shows the grade (for example N-P-K numbers), the producer and the weight, and that the contents look like the product (even granules, no wet lumps, no dust or stones).
Whatever you buy, follow the label for gloves, mask and washing, and keep chemicals away from food, children and animals.

report_note: To report a suspected fake or banned product, tell NAFDAC through its official website (nafdac.gov.ng) or its state office. Contact numbers are not listed here because we could not verify them from an official source. You can also send a private report in this app: only you and the app administrators can see it.
